files.description: The architectural invariants this repository is built around, plus the TypeScript and tooling constraints. Read this before judging whether a change is correct — several patterns that look fine in ordinary TypeScript are wrong here.

The threat model. Explains why just evaluates code at parse time and why reading a Justfile with the CLI is arbitrary code execution. Essential context for any change touching process spawning or workspace trust.
Commit conventions, PR expectations, and the procedure for adding parser support for a new just construct.

The differential harness: how our parser output is reduced to a comparable shape and checked against `just --dump --dump-format json`. Reference when reviewing changes to the parser or the semantic model.
Token kinds and spans. Shows the frozen-object-plus-union idiom used throughout in place of enums.

The single trust-checked helper every `just` subprocess spawn must go through. The canonical implementation of the trust-gating rule described in SECURITY.md and rules.md — reference when reviewing any change that spawns a process or reads `just.executablePath`.
